questions.question: Pipelines as a means of transport are looked after by the _______ of the Government of India.

options.text: Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas
Ministry of Road Transport and Highways

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas** is responsible for the exploration, production, refining, distribution, marketing, import, export, and conservation of petroleum, natural gas, petroleum products, and liquefied natural gas in India.
 
• The Ministry oversees the planning, development, and implementation of policies and programs to ensure the efficient and sustainable use of these resources.
 
• The development and maintenance of pipelines for the transportation of petroleum and natural gas fall under the purview of this Ministry.
 
• It ensures the security of supply, promotes energy efficiency, and aims to reduce the environmental impact of the petroleum and natural gas sectors.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas** formulates and implements policies for the exploration and exploitation of hydrocarbons in India.
 
• It is responsible for attracting investments in the sector and ensuring the availability of petroleum products at reasonable prices.
 
• The Ministry also promotes research and development in the petroleum and natural gas sector to enhance efficiency and sustainability.
 
• It collaborates with international organizations and other countries to secure energy resources and promote global energy security.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution mentions that a person may be appointed as the Governor of two or more states?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 153**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 153** of the Indian Constitution mentions that a person may be appointed as the Governor of two or more states.
 
• This provision allows for administrative convenience and efficiency in the governance of states.
 
• The appointment of the Governor is done by the President of India.
 
• In cases where a single individual is appointed as the Governor of multiple states, the individual exercises the powers and functions of the Governor in each of those states separately.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Constitution of India** was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on **26th November 1949 **and **came into effect on 26th January 1950**.
 
• It lays down the framework defining fundamental **political principles, establishes the structure, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions**, and sets out fundamental rights, directive principles, and the duties of citizens.
 
• The Constitution of India is the **longest written **constitution of any country in the world.
 
• It declares India a **sovereign, socialist, secular, and democratic republic, assuring its citizens justice, equality, and liberty, and endeavors to promote fraternity.**
 
• The **Seventh Schedule **of the Constitution contains three lists which delineate the subjects under the **Union, State, and Concurrent lists**.
 
• Amendments to the Constitution can be made through a process outlined in **Article 368**.
 
• The Union List has been amended several times to meet the evolving needs of the nation.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution mentions that ‘The Council of Ministers shall be collectively responsible to the Legislative Assembly of the state’?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 164(2)**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Article **164(2)** of the Indian Constitution states that the **Council of Ministers shall be collectively responsible to the Legislative Assembly of the state**.
 
• This means that the entire Council of Ministers, including the Chief Minister, is answerable to the Legislative Assembly for its actions and decisions.
 
• If the Legislative Assembly passes a vote of no confidence against the Council of Ministers, the entire council, including the Chief Minister, must resign.
 
• This provision ensures accountability and collective responsibility of the executive branch to the legislature.
 
• It reflects the principle of parliamentary democracy, where the executive is drawn from and accountable to the legislature.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Indian Constitution, adopted on **26th November 1949** and effective from **26th January 1950**, establishes the framework for the political principles, structures, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions.
 
• It is the **longest written constitution** of any country, detailing the fundamental rights, directive principles, and duties of citizens.
 
• India is declared a **sovereign, socialist, secular, and democratic republic**, ensuring justice, equality, and liberty for its citizens.
 
• The **Seventh Schedule** of the Constitution divides subjects into Union, State, and Concurrent lists, delineating the powers of the central and state governments.
 
• The Constitution can be amended as per the provisions of **Article 368**.
 
• Provisions like Article 164(2) are crucial for maintaining the balance of power and ensuring the functioning of a responsible government.

questions.question: When the President of India keeps a bill (except money bill and constitutional amendment bill) pending for an indefinite period, it is called ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**pocket veto of the President**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **A pocket veto** is the term used when the **Indian president **delays a law indefinitely. 
 
• A pocket veto is a type of legislative technique that permits the president to veto a bill without actually acting on it. This basically vetoes the law without giving it a positive vote. 
 
• The bill is neither rejected by the president nor sent back for more examination. The President is not subject to a time constraint under the Constitution to act on the bill. 
 
• Gyani Zail Singh was the first president to exercise a pocket veto.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• When a president receives a measure and is unable to reject it and send it back to Congress within ten days, this is known as a pocket veto.
 
• Despite the absence of official objections and a signature, the bill does not become law.
 
• The veto override procedure in Congress does not apply to pocket vetoes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• A simple majority can override a suspensive veto, sometimes referred to as a suspensory veto.
 
• The ability to refuse to provide the president of India's consent to a measure that has been passed by parliament is known as the absolute veto.
 
• The president can offer suggestions for improving a measure through an amendatory veto. Within ten days of the bill's passing, the president is required to veto it.

questions.question: In the Indian political system, the real executive power is vested in _________.

options.text: the Prime Minister and his Council of Ministers

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**the Prime Minister and his Council of Ministers**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Real executive power vests in a Council of Minister with the Prime Minister as the head.**
 
• **Article 74(1) **of the Constitution provides that there shall be a Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister to aid and advise the President who shall, in the exercise of his functions, act in accordance with such advice.
 
• The **Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha, the House of the People**.
 
• Thus, it is clear that the real executive power under the Constitution of India rests with the Prime Minister and his council.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In the states, the Governor, as the representative of the President, is the head of the Executive, but real executive power rests with the Chief Minister who heads the Council of Ministers.
 
• The Council of Ministers of a state is collectively responsible to the elected legislative assembly of the state.
 
• The Constitution governs the sharing of legislative power between Parliament and the State Legislatures and provides for the vesting of residual powers in Parliament.
 
• The power to amend the Constitution also vests in Parliament.
 
• The Union Executive consists of the President, the Vice-President and Council of Ministers with the Prime Minister at the head to aid and advise the President.

questions.question: Who has the power to make law and policies for the country, as per the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The Parliament.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The I**ndian Parliament** is defined under** Article 79** of the Constitution, which states that it consists of the** President of India**, **Lok Sabha** (House of the People), and **Rajya Sabha** (Council of States).
 
• The **Parliament** has the authority to legislate on subjects listed in the **Union List** (including defense, foreign affairs, and banking) and the Concurrent List (shared with states), as outlined in the **Seventh Schedule** of the Constitution.
 
• A **Money Bill** can only be introduced in the **Lok Sabha**, as per **Article 110** of the Constitution. **The Rajya Sabha** can only make recommendations on a **Money Bill,** which the Lok Sabha may accept or reject.
 
• In case of a **legislative deadlock** between the two houses, a** joint sitting of the Parliament** can be called by the **President of India**, as per **Article 108** of the Constitution, to resolve the disagreement.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Prime Minister of India** is appointed by the **President of India** as per **Article 75** of the Constitution. The Prime Minister is usually **the leader of the majority party** or coalition in the Lok Sabha.
 
• The **Prime Minister** is the head of the government and leads the Council of Ministers, which is collectively responsible to the **Lok Sabha (Article 75)**.
 
• **Political pressure **groups are organized groups that influence government policies without seeking to control the government directly. They work through lobbying, protests, and media campaigns.
 
• **Pressure groups** in India can be classified into different types such as **Business Groups** (e.g., FICCI), **Trade Unions** (e.g., AITUC), and **Professional Groups **(e.g., Bar Council of India).
 
• **Political parties** are organized groups that seek to capture power through elections by contesting in electoral processes at various levels—**national, state, or local.**
 
• The** Election Commission of India** recognizes **political parties** as either** national **or **state** parties based on specific criteria, such as the **percentage of votes or seats won in elections.**

questions.question:
Who among the following are eligible for free legal aid under the National Legal Services Authority?

A. A member of a Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe.

B. A victim of trafficking in human beings or beggar as referred to in Article 23 of the Constitution

C. An industrial workman

D. A person under circumstances of undeserved want such as being a victim of a mass disasters

E. To file any case in Supreme Court, if any person need free legal aid, the person’s annual income must be below 10 lakhs.

options.text: A, B, C, D and E
A, B, C and D only

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A, B, C and D only**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **A member of a Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe** is eligible for free legal aid under the National Legal Services Authority.
 
• **A victim of trafficking in human beings or beggar as referred to in Article 23 of the Constitution** is also eligible for free legal aid.
 
• **An industrial workman** qualifies for free legal aid as per the National Legal Services Authority.
 
• **A person under circumstances of undeserved want such as being a victim of mass disasters** is eligible for free legal aid.
 
• To file any case in the Supreme Court, if any person needs free legal aid, the person's annual income must be below a certain threshold, but **the specific limit of 10 lakhs is not mentioned under the eligibility criteria of the National Legal Services Authority.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **National Legal Services Authority (NALSA)** was constituted under the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987, to provide free legal services to the weaker sections of the society and to organize Lok Adalats for amicable settlement of disputes.
 
• The **objective of NALSA** is to ensure that opportunities for securing justice are not denied to any citizen by reason of economic or other disabilities.
 
• The criteria for providing free legal aid include several categories of persons such as women and children, disabled persons, victims of a mass disaster, ethnic violence, caste atrocity, flood, drought, earthquake or industrial disaster, and persons in custody, among others.

• The Vice-President acts as the presiding officer of the Rajya Sabha and ensures the smooth functioning of the house.
 
• In the absence of the Vice-President, the Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha presides over the sessions.
 
• The role of the Chairman includes maintaining order and decorum in the house, deciding on points of order, and ensuring that the debates and proceedings are conducted in accordance with the rules.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• It lays down the framework defining fundamental **political principles, establishes the structure, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions**, and sets out fundamental rights, directive principles, and the duties of citizens.
 
• The Constitution of India is the **longest written **constitution of any country in the world.
 
• It declares India a **sovereign, socialist, secular, and democratic republic, assuring its citizens justice, equality, and liberty, and endeavors to promote fraternity.**

questions.question: Which is NOT correct about the independence of the judiciary in our country?

options.text: The judiciary has the power to penalise those who are found guilty of contempt of court.
The judges are financially dependent on both the executive and legislature for their salaries and allowances.
The Constitution prescribes a very difficult procedure for removal of judges.
The legislature is not involved in the process of appointment of judges.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The judges are financially dependent on both the executive and legislature for their salaries and allowances.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points**__

 
• Independence of the judiciary means that the other organs of the government like the executive and legislature must not restrain the functioning of the judiciary in such a way that it is unable to do justice.
 
• judges must be able to perform their functions without fear or favor. 
 
• The Indian Constitution has ensured the independence of the judiciary through a number of measures.
 
• The legislature is not involved in the process of appointment of judges. Hence option 4 is correct. 
 
 
• Thus, it was believed that party politics would not play a role in the process of appointments.
 
• In order to be appointed as a judge, a person must have experience as a lawyer and/or must be well-versed in the law.
 
• The judges have a fixed tenure. 
 
 
• They hold office till reaching the age of retirement.
 
• Only in exceptional cases, judges may be removed.
 
• Security of tenure ensures that judges could function without fear or favor.
 
• The Constitution makers believed that a difficult procedure of removal would provide security of office to the members of the judiciary. **Hence option 3 is correct.**
 
 
 
• The judiciary is not financially dependent on either the executive or legislature. Hence option 2 is not correct. 
 
 
• The Constitution provides that the salaries and allowances of the judges are not subjected to the approval of the legislature.
 
• The actions and decisions of the judges are immune from personal criticism.
 
 
 
• The judiciary has the power to penalize those who are found guilty of contempt of court. Hence Option 1 is correct. 
 
 
• Parliament cannot discuss the conduct of the judges except when the proceeding to remove a judge is being carried out.
 
• This gives the judiciary independence to adjudicate without fear of being criticized.

questions.question: The National Commission on Agriculture (1976) of India has classified social forestry into how many categories?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** 3.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Social forestry** is divided into **three categories** by the **National Commission on Agriculture(1976).**
 
• These three types of forestry are** farm, rural, and urban.**
 
• **Urban forestry**:
 
 
• It is the practice of** growing and maintaining trees **on** public and privately owned properties** in and near urban areas, such as greenways, parks, avenues along streets, and green spaces for industry and commerce, among other places.
 
 
 
• **Rural forestry:**
 
 
• **Agroforestry and community forestry **are promoted heavily in rural forestry.
 
• Agro-forestry is the practice of **growing food and trees on the same land,** including unused areas.
 
• It alters the **simultaneous production of food, fodder, fuel, timber, and fruit** by combining forestry and agriculture.
 
• Growing trees on** public or communal land**, such as schoolyards, highway ditches, canal banks, village pastures, and temple grounds, is known as** community forestry.**
 
 
 
• **Farm forestry:**
 
 
• Farmers are urged to plant trees on their **property to meet their family's domestic requirements.**
 
• This custom of **cultivating trees on farmland **is widespread and already in place.
 
• Farmers can use** waste land for soil conservation, wind shelters, or to offer shade** for their crops.

questions.question: How many times has the term judicial review been mentioned in the constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Not mentioned anywhere**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The Judicial review system in Indian Constitution is taken from the United States of America.
 
• The power of the Judicial Review is declared as part of the basic structure of the Indian Constitution by the Supreme Court in the Indira Gandhi vs Raj Narain Case 1975.
 
• The judicial review is the process of scrutinizing any decision or law made by the government, by the courts of the country.
 
• The term judicial review is not mentioned in the constitution of India
 
• Judicial Review is governed by the principle of “Procedure established by law” as given in Article 21 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• The president proclamation under Article 356 is not immune from Judicial Review.
 
• According to the supreme court, a Presidential proclamation under Article 356 can be scrutinised under judicial review and also be revoked if found unconstitutional.
 
• The legislature dissolved under the proclamation can be revived if it is found unconstitutional.
 
• According to Article 74 (2) of the Indian constitution, the advice given by ministers to the President cannot be inquired in any court.

questions.question: The Supreme Court of India consists of ________ judges and Chief Judges of India.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is**__33__. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Supreme Court of India originally started with a **Chief Justice of India** and** 7 judges in 1950,** making a** total of 8 judges.** 
 
• 1978: Increased to **18 judges**.
 
• 2009: Further expanded to** 31 judges**.
 
• 2019: Reached the current strength of** 34 judges** (**1 Chief __Justice + 33 judges).**

__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Recommendation by the Collegium:** The Collegium, consisting of the Chief Justice of India __(CJI) and the four senior-most judges__,__ recommends names for appointment.
 
• For the **Chief Justice**, the senior-most judge is considered.
 
 
• **Presidential Appointment:** The President of India appoints the judges based on the Collegium's recommendation and the input from the Law Ministry.
 
• This process is guided by Articles** 124 and 217** of the Indian Constitution. 
 
• The current Chief Justice of India is** **Justice Bhushan Ramkrishna Gavai (B. R. Gavai) was appointed as the 52nd Chief Justice of India on 14th May 2025 and is due to retire on 23rd November 2025, upon attaining the age of 65 years.

questions.question: After how many days of absence from Parliament without permission will a Member of Parliament be disqualified?

__
 
• A** Member of Parliament (MP)** is **disqualified** from their position if they are absent from Parliament for **60 days** without permission. 
 
• This rule is **established to ensure MPs maintain a consistent presence &** participation in parliamentary proceedings
 
• The 60-day period allows for** reasonable absences while setting a clear expectation for MPs to fulfil their duties.**
 
• This mechanism helps in **maintaining the integrity** & **functionality of the parliamentary system** by discouraging prolonged unexplained absences.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Parliament**____**​**__

 
 
• Article 79 -**122 **defines the constitution of Parliament.
 
• These articles are **mentioned in the Part V **of the Indian constitution.
 
• Parliament consists of Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha, and the President.
 
• Parliament, also called the Sansad, is the legislature of the Union.
 
• Parliament conducts three sessions in a year namely the Budget session, the Monsoon session, and the winter session

questions.question: The International Olympic Committee was established in the year ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1894.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **IOC** was founded by **Pierre de Coubertin** in **Paris** in **1894**, marking the revival of the ancient Olympic Games.
 
• The **IOC** is the supreme authority of the Olympic Movement, overseeing the organization of the Summer and Winter Olympic Games.
 
• The Olympic Games are held every **four **years, alternating between Summer and Winter editions.
 
• The **IOC **is guided by the Olympic Charter, which outlines the principles and rules governing the Olympic Movement.
 
• The** IOC **works closely with** National Olympic Committees** (NOCs) from around the world to ensure the participation of athletes in the Olympic Games.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The original Olympic Games were held in **ancient Greece** from the **8th century BC** until the **4th century AD**.
 
• **Indian Olympic Association (IOA):** The IOA is the national governing body for the Olympic Movement in** India.**
 
• **Asian Olympic Council (AOC):** The AOC is the governing body for the Olympic Movement in** Asia**.
 
• The Commonwealth Games are a multi-sport event involving athletes from **Commonwealth countries** and territories.
 
• The Asian Games are a multi-sport event involving athletes from **Asia**.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a basic feature of the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Drawn from one source**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Indian Constitution is known for its **blend of rigidity and flexibility**, allowing for amendments while maintaining core principles.
 
• It is the **lengthiest written constitution** in the world, containing numerous articles and schedules.
 
• The Constitution establishes a **parliamentary system** of government, where the executive is accountable to the legislature.
 
• It is **not drawn from one source**; rather, it incorporates elements from various other constitutions around the world.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Constitution of India was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on **26th November 1949** and came into effect on **26th January 1950**.
 
• It lays down the framework defining fundamental political principles, establishes the structure, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions, and sets out fundamental rights, directive principles, and the duties of citizens.
 
• The Constitution declares India a sovereign, socialist, secular, and democratic republic, assuring its citizens justice, equality, and liberty, and endeavors to promote fraternity.
 
• The Seventh Schedule of the Constitution contains three lists which delineate the subjects under the Union, State, and Concurrent lists.
 
• Amendments to the Constitution can be made through a process outlined in Article 368.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT correct about the power of the Speaker of the state Legislative Assembly?

options.text: He maintains order and decorum of the House.
He decides whether a Bill is a Money Bill or not.
He calls for a joint session of the Assembly and Council to resolve the deadlock between the two Houses over an ordinary Bill.
He adjourns the Assembly or suspends the meeting in the absence of a quorum.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**He calls for a joint session of the Assembly and Council to resolve the deadlock between the two Houses over an ordinary Bill**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__ **

__
 
• The Speaker of the Legislative assembly conducts the business in house and decides whether a bill is a money bill or not.
 
• He maintain discipline and decorum in the house and can punish a member for unruly behavior by suspending them.
 
• He's official role is to moderate the debate, make rulings on procedure, announce the results of votes.
 
• He decides who may speak and has the power to discipline members who break the procedures of the chamber or house.
 
• He decides whether a **Bill is a Money Bill or not**.
 
• There is **no provision in constitution** for a joint session of state legislative assembly in case of deadlock between the two house over an ordinary bill.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** __**Imp articles**__

 
• **Article 178**- Deals with the Speaker/Deputy Speaker of State Legislature.
 
• **Article 182**- Deals with the chairman/Deputy Chairman' of State Legislative Council.
 
• **Article 164**- Deals with the appointment of the council of Ministers and the Chief Minister'.

questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution mentions that all executive actions of the Government of India shall be expressed to be taken in the name of the President?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 77**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 77 of the Constitution of India **pertains to the Conduct of business of the Government of India and outlines several provisions:

 
 
• All executive actions of the Government of India must be expressed to be taken in the name of the President.
 
• Orders and other instruments made and executed in the name of the President must be authenticated in a manner specified by rules established by the President.
 
• The validity of such orders or instruments, when properly authenticated, cannot be challenged on the grounds of not being made or executed by the President.
 
• The President is authorized to create rules for the more convenient transaction of the Government of India's business and for the distribution of this business among Ministers. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Article 81** of the Indian Constitution outlines the composition of the Lok Sabha, or the House of the People. It stipulates that the Lok Sabha shall consist of not more than 550 members, of whom not less than 20 shall represent the Union Territories.
 
• **Article 67** of the Constitution states the procedure for the removal of the Vice President. According to this article, the Vice President can be removed from office by a resolution passed by the Rajya Sabha with an effective majority (i.e., a majority of the total membership of the House), and agreed to by the Lok Sabha with a simple majority (i.e., a majority of the members present and voting).
 
• **Article 48** of the Constitution of India is one of the Directive Principles of State Policy. It directs the state to endeavor to prohibit the slaughter of cows, calves, and other milch and draught cattle, thereby promoting their protection and welfare.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution states that “There shall be a High Court for each state”?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 214**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 214** of the Indian Constitution states that "There shall be a High Court for each state."
 
• Each state in India has its own High Court which is the principal civil court of original jurisdiction in the state.
 
• The High Court primarily deals with cases involving civil, criminal, and constitutional law.
 
• The High Courts have the power to issue writs for enforcing fundamental rights and for any other purpose.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Constitution of India** was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on **26th November 1949** and **came into effect on 26th January 1950**.
 
• It lays down the framework defining fundamental **political principles, establishes the structure, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions**, and sets out fundamental rights, directive principles, and the duties of citizens.
 
• The Constitution of India is the **longest written** constitution of any country in the world.
 
• It declares India a **sovereign, socialist, secular, and democratic republic, assuring its citizens justice, equality, and liberty, and endeavors to promote fraternity.**
 
• The **High Courts** play a crucial role in the Indian judiciary system, serving as the intermediate appellate courts between the lower courts and the Supreme Court of India.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements are correct regarding the jurisdiction of the Supreme Court of India?

A. Original jurisdiction extends to any dispute between the Government of India and one or more States or between the Government of India and any State or States on one side and one or more States on the other or between two or more States.

B. Appellate Jurisdiction extends when the Union plus some States are one side and some other States on the other side of the dispute.

C. Under Articles 129 and 142 of the Constitution, the Supreme Court has been vested with the power to punish for contempt of court.

D. As of now, the International Commercial Arbitration cannot be initiated in the Supreme Court.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**3) A and C only**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Original Jurisdiction:** Statement A is correct. The Supreme Court's original jurisdiction extends to any dispute between the Government of India and one or more States or between the Government of India and any State or States on one side and one or more States on the other or between two or more States.
 
• **Contempt of Court:** Statement C is also correct. Under Articles 129 and 142 of the Constitution, the Supreme Court has been vested with the power to punish for contempt of court.
 
• Statement B is incorrect because the appellate jurisdiction does not extend to disputes where the Union and some States are on one side and other States are on the other side.
 
• Statement D is incorrect as the Supreme Court can entertain international commercial arbitration matters under its jurisdiction.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Supreme Court of India is the highest judicial forum and final court of appeal under the Constitution of India.
 
• It has extensive powers in the form of original, appellate, and advisory jurisdictions.
 
• The Supreme Court's decisions are binding on all other courts within the territory of India.
 
• The Supreme Court can also transfer cases from one High Court to another and even from one subordinate court to another in the interest of justice.

questions.question: In which Article does the Finance Commission of India find a mention?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 280**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Finance Commission of India is mentioned in **Article 280** of the Constitution of India.
 
• Article 280 mandates the President of India to constitute a Finance Commission every five years or at such earlier time as he considers necessary.
 
• The Finance Commission is responsible for making recommendations on the distribution of the net proceeds of taxes between the Centre and the States, and among the States themselves.
 
• It also advises on measures needed to augment the Consolidated Fund of a State to supplement the resources of the Panchayats and Municipalities in the state, based on the recommendations made by the State Finance Commissions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Finance Commission is a constitutional body created to address the financial relations between the Centre and the States.
 
• It ensures a fair and equitable distribution of financial resources between the Centre and the States, which is crucial for maintaining fiscal federalism in India.
 
• The recommendations made by the Finance Commission are advisory in nature, but they carry significant weight in the formulation of fiscal policies.
 
• The first Finance Commission was established in 1951 under the chairmanship of K.C. Neogy.
 
• The Finance Commission also reviews the state of finances of the Union and State Governments and suggests measures for maintaining a stable and sustainable fiscal environment.
